key_insight: LeapQuant shows that recurrent state in linear-attention LLMs can be quantized much more efficiently without sacrificing accuracy. It targets the hidden bottleneck in long-context inference: repeatedly reading and updating the fixed-size state.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the inference cost of linear-attention models like GDN and KDA, where the recurrent state must be accessed at every step. Naive quantization can speed things up but often hurts model quality due to accumulated errors over long sequences.
method: Designs a quantization approach tailored to recurrent state updates in linear attention models.
Reduces memory bandwidth and compute cost while preserving the fidelity of the state across many timesteps.
Focuses on limiting error accumulation so long-context performance remains stable.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, LeapQuant offers a practical path to faster and more efficient long-context LLM inference. It is especially relevant for deployment settings where memory bandwidth, latency, and quality must all be balanced.
visual_elements: Before/after pipeline diagram showing unquantized vs quantized recurrent state updates
A bottleneck icon highlighting repeated state read/write operations
Line chart of accuracy vs. sequence length comparing baseline and LeapQuant
Memory/computation comparison bars showing reduced inference cost
paper_title: LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization
paper_authors: Yi Pan, Haocheng Xi, Kan Zhu, Xingyang Li, Yibo Wu
